image_depicts: Palais de l'Université de Nancy (Building E, Faculté de Droit) at Cours Léopold, Nancy -- a current, actively-used Université de Lorraine facility, ornate 19th-c. facade with central clock, arched entrance, bare trees, winter street scene
disagreement_reason: Original candidate depicted the former University of Pont-a-Mousson (a Jesuit institution founded 1572, dissolved/relocated in 1768 -- roughly 250+ years before Universite de Lorraine was formed in 2012), a genuine but very distant lineage predecessor with no current operational connection, located in a different town (Pont-a-Mousson, ~30km from Nancy) from any campus the modern university actually operates. Original researcher itself flagged this as a judgment call rather than asserting it was correct. Independent verdict: for a 'what does this university look like today' profile photo, a 450-year-lapsed predecessor building is materially misleading, closer to a wrong-building problem than a heritage nuance. Found a clean, clearly-current, clearly-titled replacement (Palais de l'Universite de Nancy / Faculte de Droit Bat E, Cours Leopold) via Commons Category:Universite_de_Lorraine, CC BY-SA 4.0, verified URL resolves (6.1MB, 4592x3056).
notes: Replacement is a real photo of an actively-used central Nancy building housing the Faculte de Droit; Commons structured data explicitly tags it Universite de Lorraine + Palais de l'Universite de Nancy.
